examples.knowledge_point: Determining a Rate of Change Given a Related Rate and an Explicit Function
examples.problem: Given that $y=x^3+e^x$ for $x=x(t),$ and that $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d t}=2$ at the point where $x=1,$ find $\dfrac{\textrm d x}{\textrm d t}.$
examples.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={x}^{3}+{e}^{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{3}+{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}+{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (3{x}^{2}+{e}^{x}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d t}=2$ and $x=1,$ and solve for $\dfrac{\textrm d x}{\textrm d t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (3\cdot {1}^{2}+{e}^{1}) \\ 2 & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (3+e) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{2}{3+e}.\end{aligned}
$$
